key_insight: Routing user natural-language queries to the correct enterprise database is significantly harder as repositories grow and overlap; explicitly modeling schema coverage, structural connectivity, and fine-grained semantic alignment improves routing robustness.
problem_solved: Determines which database(s) in a multi-database enterprise should handle a given natural-language query, especially under domain overlap and query ambiguity.
method: Construct realistic multi-database routing benchmarks by extending existing NL-to-SQL datasets to simulate large, overlapping enterprise DB repositories.

Model routing using three complementary signals: schema coverage (which tables/columns are mentioned), structural connectivity (how schemas link across DBs), and fine-grained semantic alignment (query-to-schema meaning matching).
Evaluate routing difficulty and performance, showing degradation with larger/overlapping repositories and motivating structured, reasoning-based routing solutions.
impact: Improves reliability of NL interfaces to enterprise data platforms by reducing incorrect query dispatch, lowering latency and downstream errors; guides practitioners to design routing systems that combine structural and semantic reasoning rather than relying on surface similarity alone.
visual_elements: Schematic pipeline: user query → routing model (coverage + connectivity + semantic alignment) → selected database(s)
Heatmap or line chart showing routing accuracy drop as repository size and domain overlap increase
Diagram of two overlapping schema graphs with highlighted cross-schema links to illustrate structural connectivity
Bar chart comparing baseline heuristics vs. the proposed multi-signal routing approach on benchmark metrics
paper_title: Routing End User Queries to Enterprise Databases
paper_authors: Saikrishna Sudarshan, Tanay Kulkarni, Manasi Patwardhan, Lovekesh Vig, Ashwin Srinivasan
